title: RunEvent
description: One record of a run, in the order the runtime wrote it. The runtime's own record is carried unchanged, as an opaque document; the daemon adds the run, the session, two numbers and the time. `sequence` counts per run, `position` counts per daemon over all runs: the stream's event id is the position, and a client resumes after the last position it saw.

session_id.description: The session of the run, copied from it by the handler when it records the event; absent for a run of no session. It is what lets the events of a session be paged by position.

sequence.description: Per run, from 1; each later event of the run has a larger number.

position.description: Per daemon, from 1, strictly increasing over all runs; minted by the daemon when it records the event.

record.description: The runtime's record, byte for byte as a document; no secret appears in it (design sheet, decision 10).

sdc.daemon.EventId.title: EventId
sdc.daemon.EventId.description: The id the daemon gives a recorded event. It is the row's identity only; the stream's id is the event's position.

sdc.daemon.EventKind.title: EventKind
sdc.daemon.EventKind.description: Open text: the kind of the runtime's run-log line, copied. Events the daemon writes itself have a kind that starts with `runbook.`, and the command that writes each one declares it: runbook.submitted (SubmitRun), runbook.cancel-requested (CancelRun), runbook.start-failed (FailRunStart), runbook.run-orphaned (EndOrphanedRun), runbook.answer-undeliverable (AnswerDecision) and runbook.runtime-failed (written by the daemon just before it issues EndRun with the outcome runtime-failure) and runbook.action-started (written by the daemon when the runtime tells that a program of an action, or its `handoff_when` check, is about to start, before the program starts; record: case, action, role (`program` or `check`) and try, each absent when unknown; the language cannot write a RunEvent from a command, so it is stated here, and the view RunDetail shows the step while the program runs). Not a closed set for the runtime's own kinds.

sdc.daemon.RunId.title: RunId
sdc.daemon.RunId.description: The id of a run. The daemon mints it (a UUID, version 7) in the HTTP handler and returns it in the answer to the submit; the handler fills the `run_id` input of SubmitRun and a client never chooses it. The state directory of the run is named after it. A run id that is already taken cannot occur, because the daemon mints it; the specification has no refusal for it.

sdc.daemon.SessionId.title: SessionId
sdc.daemon.SessionId.description: The name of a session, chosen by the client that opens it.
